policy_contract: FROZEN policy only (confirmed_dd_guard, v29-iso4 chain). No threshold/architecture/frequency/ensemble changes. This module repairs the R77 runner-level rolling/state interface only; strategy/execution semantics are imported UNMODIFIED from scripts/opencode_r77_advisor_core.py.

timeliness_policy.stale_after_description: signals older than 24 closed 5-minute bars (2h) past their decision bar are DIAGNOSTIC-only, never actionable alerts/intents
timeliness_policy.rationale: Pre-specified BEFORE implementation. N-decay ladder evidence (round10 v40: edge survives to d24/2h at +89%, dead at d48/4h) bounds the honest actionability horizon at (2h,4h]; 24 bars is the conservative end. Stale catch-up must never be presented as a timely new alert.
timeliness_policy.enforcement: decision_time more than stale_after_bars*bar_seconds behind the current observation instant, OR decision exec-index more than stale_after_bars behind the current settling exec-index, forces DIAGNOSTIC-only (gates untouched).

reconcile.identity: market (symbol/interval) + open_time UTC; positional-index modulo FORBIDDEN
reconcile.clock: 6h UTC grid from open_time via r77 core.on_grid (absolute grid, never positional)
reconcile.gap_policy: NEVER silently bridge missing execution bars: gaps are recorded as gap events with exact missing range; no synthetic bars are ever settled
reconcile.revision_policy: historical OHLC revision on an already-settled bar is recorded as a revision event; the settled record is kept (no silent overwrite, no re-settlement)
reconcile.forming_policy: bars with close_time > observed_at are forming and excluded
reconcile.nonfinite_policy: bars with non-finite OHLC/volume are rejected (INCOMPLETE)

bootstrap.rule: bootstrap history is diagnostic-only: every inference with decision_time <= shadow_start is DIAGNOSTIC (gates untouched, never an actionable alert/intent)

checkpoint.scheme: generation-counter + atomic rename (temp file + fsync + os.replace) + append-only JSONL journal + CURRENT pointer; exports rebuilt from journal without re-emitting
checkpoint.corrupt_policy: corrupt/truncated CURRENT or checkpoint fails clearly (names the file+generation) or recovers from the last verified generation; never resume on unverified bytes

identity_verification.rule: hash actual file BYTES on resume (never accept a declared hash when bytes differ); any change forces an explicit new run (refuse resume naming the field)
identity_verification.note: checkpoint/calibrator model bytes listed in the prespec are also hashed when present on disk; missing model files fail closed (no stub substitution in production paths)
